baseline.governing_rule: NEW BEHAVIOR = EXISTING VERIFIED BEHAVIOR + EXPLICIT REQUESTED DELTA

principles.name: Engineering/developer authority
principles.definition: Product intent, architecture, acceptance and final change authority remain human-owned; AI execution is delegated only inside approved boundaries.
principles.trigger: Every TCAF operation.

principles.name: Evidence and repository state before unsupported assumptions
principles.definition: Use repository/project evidence rather than chat memory. Canonical documents govern approved intent/lifecycle state; implementation evidence governs observed implementation state.
principles.trigger: Whenever TCAF reasons about project state, task state, capability state or implementation state.
principles.notes: 0.4 distinguishes canonical approved state from observed implementation evidence. Semantic-model BLACK_BOX acceptance for 040-05 project-sync verified read-only drift inspection/proposal and explicitly bounded canonical reconciliation while preserving unresolved evidence; implementation, verification, and health remain partial because the principle applies across all applicable operations.

principles.name: Explicit bounded scope and change surface
principles.definition: Every executable change has an explicit goal, authorized edit surface, allowed change types and stop conditions.
principles.trigger: Every operation that may authorize or describe change.

principles.name: Explicit permission
principles.definition: Permission is explicit; an unapproved file or change type is not implicitly authorized.
principles.trigger: Whenever TCAF defines or executes an authorized change surface.

principles.name: Minimum-first instructions and prompts
principles.definition: Use the shortest safe instruction set that preserves all applicable behavior; add detail only when evidence shows it is needed.
principles.trigger: Every runtime composition and model-facing instruction surface.

principles.name: Selective context loading
principles.definition: Inspect and load only target evidence and framework guidance relevant to the current operation.
principles.trigger: Every runtime composition and target inspection step.

principles.name: Preservation-first
principles.definition: Compatible working behavior, local patterns, developer edits and project evidence are preserved unless an approved change explicitly targets them.
principles.trigger: Whenever existing project material, behavior or developer work may be affected.

principles.name: Existing capabilities only
principles.definition: Libraries, scripts, tools, architecture, infrastructure and capabilities are available only when verified or explicitly approved.
principles.trigger: Whenever planning or execution depends on a project capability.

principles.name: Reuse before adding
principles.definition: Reuse compatible existing functions, guards, validations, utilities and local patterns before introducing new equivalents.
principles.trigger: Whenever implementation or planning proposes functionality already partially represented in the project.

custom.policy: Project conventions may refine preferred reuse patterns, but preservation and avoidance of unnecessary duplication cannot be waived.

principles.name: Implementation source hierarchy
principles.definition: Existing projects follow verified compatible local patterns first; absent a usable local pattern, use compatible official documentation, then established ecosystem practice.
principles.trigger: Whenever TCAF must choose how a change should be implemented.

principles.name: No silent conflict
principles.definition: Security, correctness, compatibility or authoritative-state conflicts are surfaced and resolved explicitly.
principles.trigger: Whenever evidence or instructions conflict materially.

principles.name: Smallest useful coherent change
principles.definition: A task or step is the smallest useful complete, bounded and verifiable change that leaves a valid project state; task count and line count are not optimization targets.
principles.trigger: Whenever TCAF creates, evaluates or decomposes a unit of work.

custom.policy: Approved project decomposition policy may refine task boundaries but may not waive boundedness, coherence, reviewability or verification.

principles.name: Explicit refactor authorization
principles.definition: Refactoring or restructuring requires explicit authorization and is not implied by feature, fix, planning or adoption work.
principles.trigger: Whenever proposed work could restructure working logic or architecture.

principles.name: Evidence-based verification and claims
principles.definition: Validation and verification claims are evidence records, not predictions; PASS requires executed successful authoritative checks for the declared scope.
principles.trigger: Whenever TCAF reports validation, verification or check results.

principles.name: AI self-check is not human acceptance
principles.definition: Agent self-checks may provide evidence but cannot substitute for developer/team review and acceptance.
principles.trigger: Every operation with a review or acceptance gate.

principles.name: Lifecycle states remain distinct
principles.definition: Implementation, verification, review/acceptance and commit are distinct lifecycle evidence and must not be inferred from one another.
principles.trigger: Whenever task or feature lifecycle state is read, written or reported.

principles.name: Live workspace state and concurrent-change preservation
principles.definition: Re-read current relevant files after pauses or external edits and preserve compatible developer or concurrent changes.
principles.trigger: Whenever work resumes after a pause, external edit or concurrent change.

principles.name: Immutable executed history and historical identities
principles.definition: Completed task scope and historical identifiers remain stable; later fixes, extensions or refactors are linked rather than retroactively rewriting history.
principles.trigger: Whenever existing completed work or historical task identifiers are encountered.

principles.name: Explicit active-task change classification
principles.definition: Clarification, correction, local adaptation, amendment, separate request and blocker are distinct and produce different authorization behavior.
principles.trigger: Whenever an approved or active task receives a new request, correction or conflict.

principles.name: Outcome-first operational interaction
principles.definition: Operational responses begin with outcome, completed action and next developer step; extra explanation is included only when useful.
principles.trigger: Every operational response.

principles.name: Tool resilience
principles.definition: The workflow remains valid when an agent cannot directly run commands or edit files; permissions and evidence adapt to actual host capabilities.
principles.trigger: Every run regardless of adapter capabilities.

principles.name: Deterministic runtime and module resolution
principles.definition: Operations resolve through registered agents, machine-authoritative manifests, safe module paths, one target and one adapter.
principles.trigger: Every runtime run-envelope assembly.

principles.name: Framework instructions and target evidence remain separate
principles.definition: Framework modules define procedure; target-project artifacts are evidence. Neither surface is silently reclassified as the other.
principles.trigger: Every run that combines framework instructions with a target.

principles.name: Adapters change transport, not semantics
principles.definition: Adapters may change transport and available tool access only; they do not alter core rules, manifest behavior, permissions or output schema.
principles.trigger: Every run through any adapter.

principles.name: Team and multi-agent capable workflow
principles.definition: Planning and execution support separate ownership, parallel contributors/agents and integration gates without assuming one executor or one architectural layer.
principles.trigger: Whenever work may have multiple owners, agents, workstreams or independently executable units.
principles.notes: Semantic-model BLACK_BOX acceptance confirms the planner's profile handling, parallel readiness, no-invented-ownership behavior, and review-gate convergence. Detailed/specialist team execution guidance remains partial and optional, so full BP-25 BLACK_BOX verification is still required.

principles.name: Organizational execution profile
principles.definition: A project may declare single-developer, team, or multi-team. When unspecified, planning remains team-capable and must not invent serial technical dependencies.
principles.trigger: Whenever planning or execution organization is known or materially affects ownership and execution shape.

custom.policy: Valid organizational profiles are unspecified, single-developer, team or multi-team. In the absence of an approved profile, planning resolves to the unspecified team-capable default. The principle itself is not waivable.

principles.notes: Semantic-model BLACK_BOX acceptance covered the unspecified, single-developer, team, and multi-team organizational profiles, plus approved custom decomposition mode, without external corrective prompts; deterministic tests remain separate evidence.

principles.name: Feature is not Task
principles.definition: A feature/outcome is a planning unit that may contain one or more tasks and uses a separate identity namespace by default.
principles.trigger: Whenever a requested outcome or feature is planned or related to task state.
principles.notes: Semantic-model BLACK_BOX acceptance confirmed separate feature/task identities and allocation from the feature namespace; deterministic tests remain separate evidence.

principles.name: Architecture-aware decomposition
principles.definition: Task boundaries derive from the actual architecture, responsibilities and coherent outcomes rather than hard-coded frontend/backend/shared layers.
principles.trigger: Whenever an operation creates, changes or evaluates task decomposition.

custom.policy: Approved project planning/decomposition policy may refine decomposition heuristics but may not override non-waivable TCAF invariants.

principles.notes: Planner-specific semantic-model BLACK_BOX acceptance passed for architecture-aware task boundaries. Broader PLAN-family implementation and verification remain incomplete.

principles.name: Dependencies are semantic, not ordinal
principles.definition: A dependency exists only for a real prerequisite, contract, capability, blocker or other semantic requirement; task number, roadmap order, phase order or one-person schedule do not create dependencies.
principles.trigger: Whenever dependencies, blockers or next-executable work are derived.
principles.notes: Planner-specific semantic-model BLACK_BOX acceptance passed for real prerequisites and schedule-independent dependencies. Broader WORK-family implementation and verification remain incomplete.

principles.name: Dependency DAG and parallel-ready work
principles.origin: 0.4 feature planning plus historical team semantics
principles.definition: Planning represents real prerequisite relationships as an acyclic graph and may expose multiple simultaneously executable tasks when no true dependency blocks them.
principles.trigger: Whenever work ordering, readiness or parallel execution is planned.
principles.notes: Planner-specific semantic-model BLACK_BOX acceptance passed for semantic DAG preservation and parallel-ready work. Broader WORK-family implementation and verification remain incomplete.

principles.name: Shared contracts are contextual decomposition signals
principles.origin: explicit 0.4 semantic change from historical team rule
principles.definition: A shared contract or interface becomes a dedicated task only when it is itself a coherent independently reviewable outcome or materially unlocks independent workstreams.
principles.trigger: Whenever a shared contract, schema, interface or boundary is considered during decomposition.
principles.notes: Semantic-model BLACK_BOX acceptance verified both contextual directions: no automatic shared-boundary task, and a dedicated boundary task when independently reviewable/verifiable or materially workstream-unlocking.

principles.name: Explicit convergence when integration work is real
principles.origin: historical team integration, extended in 0.4 planning
principles.definition: Convergence/integration is represented explicitly when independently produced work must genuinely be reconciled, integrated or jointly verified; no ceremonial convergence task is required otherwise.
principles.trigger: Whenever independent workstreams must be brought together or jointly validated.

principles.name: Feature member, prerequisite and platform capability are distinct
principles.definition: Planning distinguishes feature-member work from external prerequisites, already available capabilities and cross-cutting/platform capabilities.
principles.trigger: Whenever feature planning classifies existing or missing work.
principles.notes: Semantic-model BLACK_BOX acceptance confirmed feature-member, external-prerequisite, existing-capability, and unrelated-work classification in planner scenarios. Generalized platform/cross-cutting capability handling still requires behavioral hardening.

principles.name: Task verification is not feature acceptance
principles.definition: A task may be verified or accepted while its parent feature remains incomplete; feature acceptance requires separate feature-level satisfaction.
principles.trigger: Whenever task lifecycle evidence is interpreted in feature-level planning or acceptance.

principles.name: Canonical intended state and actual implementation evidence are distinct
principles.definition: Canonical state represents approved intent/lifecycle state; repository/configuration evidence represents observed implementation state. A mismatch is drift and must be surfaced rather than silently resolved.
principles.trigger: Whenever canonical documentation and observed repository/configuration state may disagree.
principles.notes: Semantic-model BLACK_BOX acceptance confirmed that planner canonical/documentation drift is surfaced rather than silently resolved. 040-05 project-sync acceptance also verified explicit reconciliation of canonical intended state and observed repository evidence, including unresolved planned-task impact outside approved writes. This is scoped sync evidence only; implementation remains PARTIAL and verification/health remain REVIEW_REQUIRED pending broader cross-operation coverage.

principles.name: Validator authority is bounded to its declared domain
principles.definition: The runtime validator is authoritative only for the canonical framework/project structure it validates; it does not prove product behavior, business correctness, task acceptance or feature completion.
principles.trigger: Whenever validator output is used as evidence.

principles.name: Applicable principles propagate across relevant operations
principles.definition: A principle applies because its semantic trigger is true, not because a particular specialist file happened to be loaded. Every relevant operation must preserve applicable principles while still using minimum necessary model context.
principles.trigger: Every operation and stage during applicability resolution and model-context composition.
principles.notes: Deterministic compact runtime propagation is implemented and includes sync. The 040-05 semantic-model BLACK_BOX exercised sync behavior only, not a cross-operation propagation matrix, so it does not promote BP-37 verification or health.

semantics: Absent custom policy: use TCAF standard architecture-aware decomposition.
Approved custom policy: the project/team may refine task grouping, ownership conventions, decomposition examples and organization.
Custom policy may not waive bounded scope, preservation-first, reviewability, meaningful verification, semantic dependency correctness, explicit refactor authorization or human acceptance.
